literal: Envious heart-he-of prosperity-and, upright-man-of ruin-and, to-ponder will-be.
translation: The prosperity of a man with an envious heart, and the ruin of an upright man, are things to be deeply pondered.
modern: பொறாமை கொண்ட மனம் உடையவனின் செல்வமும், நேர்மையான மனம் உடையவனின் வறுமையும் சான்றோரால் ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்கப்படும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts two unexpected situations: an envious person gaining wealth ('ஆக்கம்') and a righteous person facing ruin ('கேடு'). The word 'அவ்விய' means crooked or envious, fitting the chapter's theme of not envying, while 'செவ்வியான்' denotes someone who is straight and upright. The phrase 'நினைக்கப் படும்' indicates that these outcomes will be deeply pondered, as they seem to contradict the natural order of justice. The text implies that such unnatural states are anomalies that provoke thought about their true causes and ultimate consequences.
